page.layout: One column of verse, set left of centre, with a signature mark centred below the last line and a catchword at the lower right.

p.i: Quos musca cum proboscide, atque vexato
Quaestus juvat labore nodus in scirpo.
Non insolens, non aucupans novos sensus,
At strenuum illud integrans sine ampullis
Tormenta per mille atque mille per mortes
Animosa virtus, sancta sed Fides terris
Heu! illa avitis dum stetit titolis, felix,
Aetas Parentum, quae sacris procul rixis,
Non glande pasta vel rudi tamen fa[?]no,
Non fece pota vel sophisticis sputis
Sed flore lactis, sed liquore Sionis
Sciri negata scire non nimis quaerens,
Nunc exul, exspes, improbisque vah! fame[?]
Nec vult videri tota, tota nec condi,

page.notes: Verse without visible stanza breaks; each printed line is given as its own paragraph. The initial "Q" of lines 1 and 2 and the "Q" of line 12 are large swash capitals. Doubtful readings: "fa[?]no" (line 22, possibly fæno) and "fame[?]" (line 29, ink blot over the word end). The signature mark at the foot reads as "II I 2" and is uncertain. The catchword "Pu-" at the lower right is partly smudged.
